newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish coalition shaky as army showdown looms.
newsitem.headline: Turkish coalition shaky as army showdown looms.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led coalition strained at the seams on Friday ahead of a showdown with generals angered by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's failure to curb a Moslem religious revival.
Erbakan, the first Islamist to lead modern Turkey, and pro-Western government ally Tansu Ciller hastily arranged a meeting amid reports the government was close to collapse.
Aides said the pair would hold talks later in the day. Ciller earlier denied a press story that she would pull out of the alliance at the behest of the powerful army.
"Don't believe things about withdrawing from the government that you haven't heard from me," she told reporters after an unscheduld leadership meeting of her True Path Party (DYP).

The army top brass is expected to confront Erbakan at a National Security Council meeting on Saturday with his failure to implement an anti-Islamist crackdown demanded by the fiercely secularist military two months ago.

Two anti-Islamist ministers from Ciller's wing are in open rebellion against Erbakan's Welfare Party for stalling on military plans to restrict religious education, penalise Islamist dress and move against Islamist business and media.
The Yeni Yuzyil daily quoted unnamed cabinet ministers as saying rightist Ciller would abandon the Islamists in fear of the True Path rebellion growing.
"The feeling among the DYP is that Ciller has definitely decided to pull out," wrote Yeni Yuzyil columnist Bilal Cetin, a respected political analyst.
Turkish stocks were little changed on Friday after falling nearly five percent the previous day on political worries.
An Islamist cabinet member acknowledged all was not well between the coalition partners.
"It's not a piece of cake but we can hardly say either that everything is over, that the government has gone," State Minister Mehmet Altinsoy told Reuters.

A war of attrition between Welfare and the army reached a new height on Thursday when the Islamists threatened legal action against a middle-ranking general who had verbally abused Erbakan in comments seen on national television.
The commander called Erbakan a "pimp" for going on pilgrimage to the Moslem holy city of Mecca as the guest of conservative Saudi King Fahd.

Military sources said the exact agenda for Saturday's meeting was not clear yet but the Turkish media has reported that an army demand to extend secularist education to eight years from the current five would be debated.
A spokesman for Ciller's party was confident Erbakan's faction would eventually back the eight-year plan, despite opposition from his grassroots.
"The matter of eight years' education will be put to parliament by the government," leading True Path member Hasan Ekinci told a news conference.
Generals have ousted three governments since 1960 but observers say it is reluctant to stage another coup partly because it would badly hit NATO member Turkey's bid to get closer to Europe.

The army is practically the only state authority in a large chunk of southeastern Turkey where troops are fighting Kurdish separatist rebels. Turkey also keeps some 30,000 troops on the divided island of Cyprus.
